citation: 12 CFR 53.4(a) (OCC, Bank A); 12 CFR 304.24(a) (FDIC, Bank B); 12 CFR 225.303(a) (FRB, same text)
trigger: The company determines it has had a computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to a bank for four or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after that determination (runbook: determination by the 2-hour mark)
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank; if none was provided, the bank's CEO and CIO (or two individuals of comparable responsibilities) by any reasonable means (53.4(a)(1)-(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Bank A and Bank B. Scheduled maintenance, testing, or software updates previously communicated to the bank are excluded (53.4(b)). No FRB-supervised customer today

obligation: Bank contract notice of unauthorized access to customer information
citation: Bank A and Bank B vendor contracts (security exhibits), implementing Interagency Guidelines Supplement A, II (12 CFR Part 30, App. B; 12 CFR Part 364, App. B)
trigger: Unauthorized access to the bank's customer information is known or suspected (for example a script ran on a bank server that holds customer data)
deadline: Within 24 hours (contract term). Supplement A says the contract should require notice as soon as possible
notify: The bank's contract security contact (same as the designated contact once collected)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both bank contracts. Applies even if the 4-hour test is not met

obligation: Banks' own notice to their regulator (context)
citation: 12 CFR 53.3 (OCC) and the parallel FDIC rule
trigger: A bank determines that a notification incident has occurred
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank's determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's duty. The company's notice and follow-up facts feed the bank's 36-hour clock

trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting the customer's services or data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's designated security contact

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), with all information it needs for its own notices under 501.171(3)-(4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent when it maintains or processes personal information for customers (501.171(1)(h))

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company itself holds (employee records; portal user names with passwords; customer contacts) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause given in writing to the department)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the company's own personal information is involved

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 15-day extension applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (unlikely: about 180 portal users and 7 employees)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (company's own data)
trigger: Company must notify more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals (unlikely at this size)

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); many states also require a service provider to notify the data owner
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Check each time. Customers' data subjects may live outside Florida; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment (for example if the script encrypted customer servers)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. The company never pays on a customer's behalf

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA incident reporting
trigger: Compromise of a tool that reaches many customers
deadline: As early as practical, as counsel advises

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: MDR provider escalation to the company (inbound)
trigger: The MDR detects a high-severity threat on a laptop, identity account, or firewall
deadline: Per the MDR contract's escalation terms (phone escalation to the on-call engineer, 24x7)
notify: On-call engineer, then the incident commander
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. The MDR does not see RMM logs until POAM-009 closes

obligation: RMM vendor incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: RMM vendor terms (no notice clause today)
trigger: The RMM vendor detects a compromise of its platform or the company's tenant
deadline: None in the current contract (gap). Target: 72 hours or less at amendment by 2026-12-31 (POAM-012)

citation: FedRAMP incident communication rules (apply only to FedRAMP-certified cloud services used by agencies)
trigger: FedRAMP reportable incident affecting federal customer data
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal customer and no FedRAMP certification (P03 G-001)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck coverage of a 7-person IT provider when final

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information or a covered contractor information system
notify: DoD (DIBNet portal); subcontractors also notify the prime
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contracts; the MSA prohibits covered defense information

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article, in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
